So we feel very comfortable with where we are today and again, a demonstration of resilience. We wanted to compare both periods to show how the company sailed through the third quarter, mostly because of the resilience of the results achieved in the first quarter and on the second quarter.

This slide demonstrates the significant cash flow that the company can deliver at current installed capacity. We are forecasting 240,000 tons for the 12 months forward. At those levels, even at current lithium prices, we can deliver approximately USD 128 million of cash flow. When one looks at the forward production we are forecasting for 2027 of 330,000 tons at current prices, we are expecting to deliver approximately $191 million of cash flow. These are robust levels and again, a direct result of our low all-in sustaining costs. So one more demonstration of operational resilience enabled by the low costs. This slide demonstrates the effect of the pivotal 5-year debt refinancing on our balance sheet.

We issued a $125 million convertible note, which had a transformational effect on the debt profile of the company. Essentially, this convertible note also creates the potential for deleveraging because it's almost at the money. The proceeds were mainly used to pay down upcoming debt maturing in December of this year, and that debt was essentially transferred to November of 2031. So it smoothed of our debt maturity profile, matching that with upcoming cash flows. On the right, when we look at the picture of the third quarter static, one can see that the pro forma operating cash flow for the year, assuming we would annualize the 9-month 2026 cash generation would still give us a low leverage ratio.

But the current issuance lowered it even further. This slide shows how transformational the 5-year convertible note was for our future growth plans. It creates low leverage ratios, essentially enabling us to create borrow capacity. So here, we show the low leverage ratios even at current lithium low prices, connecting to the cash flows we showed earlier at the 2 levels of forecasted production, one can see in yellow the leverage ratios with the convertible note unconverted. And in green, the leverage ratios of the convertible note converted. It becomes negligible.

So at either of the production levels we forecast, 240,000 tons for the next 12 months or 330,000 tons for 2027, we end up with very low leverage at $1,200 per ton. So the next page demonstrates the borrowing capacity opened up by this pivotal refinancing. And here, we pro forma the convertible note, again, converted and unconverted. Even converted at low levels of lithium, we averaged out the cash flows. We end up at 2x with extra room for borrow, let's say, at 2027 forecasted production levels of another $170 million. And at 3x leverage at 2027 forecasted production levels at $330 million. So we delevered the balance sheet.

And even with the convertible note in there at regular leverage ratios of 2x or 3x, we have ample room for borrowing. Clearly, we would not borrow in a rate that's not conducive to the nature of our business. So if we were to regear the balance sheet, we will do that with what we call adjusted debt, meaning project finance debt or development debt. But nevertheless, these are the raw numbers. And we wanted to stress this because it shows how pivotal the note was. This slide basically talks about the underpinning variable that's going to drive lithium going forward. The demand is a consensus.

The entire market is very aligned in the fact that lithium demand is growing and growing robustly. However, prices are not driven by demand. They're driven by this low-cost supply coming out of regions that are not necessarily formal. So the challenge for us producers is to remain resilient to match those prices. And this is what Sigma has demonstrated throughout this presentation. When you look at the impact of African production, there are 3 key variables. First is vertically integrated with the supply chain. So it continues to produce and deliver even during price downturn, almost in price agnostic.

Then you have the phenomenon of low-cost DSO or low concentrate DSO where the material gets to the client almost at cost given that the client is financing the production. So the only curbing is the downward pressure of high logistics costs. And then you have the full concentrate production coming out of countries like Zimbabwe and Mali, those are formal and they're integrated into the supply chain. So they come at an LCE equivalent of $7,000 to $13,000 [indiscernible] per ton. In other words, very competitive pricing. So here at Sigma, as we described, we are the floor.

So these prices don't worry us because even with this pricing environment, we can compete and we can deliver significant cash flow. Today, for instance, prices are about $1,200, which gives us ample room to deliver cash flow. So that's the importance of resilience is the fact that going forward, lithium pricing will continue to remain volatile as demand demonstrates tremendous growth throughout the next couple of years. Now we go into the production capacity and what we see as the 2026, 2027 operational outlook. This slide demonstrates how Sigma will deliver the forecast.

What we are forecasting for the 2027 year is not different than what we have already delivered since the upgrade of our industrial plant in the fourth quarter of 2024. The plant has 2 circuits, the reprocessing circuit and the main circuit. The total production capacity amounting to approximately 82,000 tons. In the fourth quarter '24, we delivered 77,000 tons. So that's industrial capacity. From then onwards, we delivered approximately 68,000 tons every single quarter. And if you annualize the third quarter when we decommissioned the contractor, it was the same exact number. Then in 2026, we entered the primarization phase, and we quickly reached the targets on the second quarter. The third quarter, we were stopped.

But again, we demonstrated tremendous resilience to just bounce back and pick up when we left off twice. We remobilized and demobilized our entire contingent twice. So when you look at the picture of the third quarter, it's essentially a company motion because we have 21,000 tons of inventory and 7,000 tons of production. Now entering the fourth quarter, we have an additional 11,000 tons of production of high grade. Going forward, as we catch up with removal of overburden, we're going to be well on our way to deliver on our projections.

This page gets further into the details of the reprocessing circuit we talked about on the previous page, where we've shown that we can deliver approximately 15,000 tons of high-grade material coming out of the circuit. This is a circuit that's separate from the main high-grade circuit. It has its own dedicated cyclones, its DMSs, and it essentially upgrades the fines into higher-grade material in an automated process so that we achieve 100% circularity, but more importantly, we deliver more lithium with the same mining footprint. That was the key to the upgrade of the lithium industrial facility, going from an average of 60,000 tonnes per quarter into 77,000 plus up to 82,000 tonnes per quarter, the reprocessing circuit.

That is the 100% circularity we strived for, making us able to meet the recycling criteria of the European Union because our lithium has recycled material, same mining footprint, more lithium. This page essentially shows how the Cleantech plant upgrade enables 100% circularity. The amount of concentrate is essentially larger with just that one plant. In other words, in the fourth quarter '24, the plant delivered 920 tonnes a day. What we're forecasting going forward is kind of in the same magnitude at 950 tonnes a day. So nothing different than what we've been delivering. And that's again, the 15,000 tonne extra coming from the reprocessing circuit is more lithium concentrate with just one plant. Here is the mining.

So we're focusing now on increasing volumes during the fourth quarter to compensate for unremoved overburden that stay put during the third quarter. We're going after the same section of the pit shell design in order to access this larger amount of high-grade material. So this is the south of our South pit. In other words, there's approximately 200,000 tons of concentrate equivalent over here, a volume of approximately 1.1 million tons of ore. And that's the goal for us in the next month or so, getting to that material, processing and converting that into concentrate. On this page is how we plan to deliver it.

We're doing a second round of fleet upgrades, bringing in larger excavators and larger trucks. The excavators deliver an additional 40% ability to load up the trucks and then the trucks deliver a 25% increased ability to haul material. So the second stage deployment of large equipment is essentially a result of the primarized and upgraded mining operations. And again, we do more haulage with fewer amount of equipment, less diesel, more efficiency. And that's a result of our partnership with SANY China and our equipment provider. We have decreased lead times for equipment availability and larger equipment available for us.

Wrapping up this section on operational delivery, we want to delve into achieving the landmark victories of our impeccable environmental and social credentials. Minas Gerais delivered the verdict that Sigma is too big to stop. We achieved this institutional visibility to our economic impact of Vale do Jequitinhonha. Rule of law has upheld our licenses and operations. So it was the institutional strength of Minas Gerais in Brazil. Rule of law swift resolution to the stoppages. We were awarded the TAC in record time, and we were awarded a classification of too big to stop and then limited financial exposure given that we didn't have any additional royalties or any essentially burdens levied on the company.

But more importantly, we came out of this with a positive engagement with the state administration and with the federal courts, demonstrating the number of jobs at risk and the number of family members that would be vulnerable if Sigma wasn't operating. We have over 19,000 jobs connected to us directly. It's a shared prosperity business model. And out of these jobs depend 80,000 people. So this is essentially the too big to stop. These are Sigma fuel jobs. Half of them come from our social engagement, social inclusion programs. Here is the object of one of the conversations, the TAC.

Ultimately, we demonstrate here that we adhere to the highest global mining standards with our Quintuple Zero fully traceable lithium. If you look at other G7 countries, you can see there are high standards. There's a tailing dams to high standards in a country, and there are overburden rock piles to high standards in another country, both G7s. When you look at Sigma and our rock piles, they have the same standards of a G7 country rock pile and they have grass -- active germination, which was our element of delivery in concomitance with the TAC. We agreed to $1 million of active germination to be delivered throughout the next year. Concluding the presentation, here are our priorities.

We plan to continue to execute and achieve the re-rating. First, the milestones for 2027. We're going to continue to ramp up mine 1. We're going to deliver on the growth, and we're going to unlock the full potential of Phase 2 in stages in a disciplined organized execution. First, continuing ramp-up of Mine 1. We plan to deliver 240,000 tonnes in the next 12 months. We're going through a second round of fleet upgrades to enable more haulage, and we plan to deliver 330,000 tons in the full year of 2027. Second, growth. We plan to resume Phase 2 growth plan with a new mine opening.

In other words, we're going to resume Phase 2 bottom-up, opening a new mine. We're fully funded for the CapEx of opening a new mine by the current cash flow generated by the existing industrial line. Why did we start by the mine? Because it's the largest job creation. That's how we bring the most amount of prosperity to Vale do Jequitinhonha. A new mine means another 25,000 people connected to Sigma, 6,400 indirect jobs, and that's without the social programs attached to it. Then we will resume Plant 2 construction. So with that, we would plan to get to 580,000 tons of capacity, which will bring in more job creation in the region.

So unlocking the full potential of Phase 2. If we start the mine, if you would add this number of jobs to the current jobs we have, we would essentially following opening a second mine, have 100,000 people connected to our operation at Jequitinhonha -- Vale do Jequitinhonha. In other words, the potential for prosperity is tremendous, and that is why we have tremendous support from the newly elected government of Brazil and Minas Gerais. And here, we have the magic. It's low cost plus cash generation. So we're very well positioned for re-rating. There are companies that have the same production that we have and that trade at double our value.

We do believe that as we continue to execute, the re-rating will come gradually. And this is why we're so focused and we maintain our discipline. And with that, I'll conclude and shall pass on to Q&A.

Operator: [Operator Instructions] Our first 3 questions comes from Ailing Chen from Hotwind. With Q3 production falling to just 7,293 tonnes, how did unit cash costs remain so low? Were shutdown-related fixed costs excluded or capitalized? This is the first question. The second question is regarding the USD 120 million convertible notes, are there any provisions that allow the company to redeem or repurchase the notes earlier to avoid shareholders' dilution? If so, could you please explain these provisions in detail, including any conditions, restrictions or early redemption penalties? And that's it.

Ana Cabral Gardner: So I'll answer questions one by one. First, it was regarding the costs. They were neither capitalized nor excluded. They sit as an expense line together with other operating expenses. There's a note specifically dealing with this, which is Note 24. So those costs amount to $13,376. And essentially, these are what we call idle capacity costs. The note provides quite a lot of detail about it. And that's how IFRS would dictate us to account for these costs. The second question is related to the convertible bond. Yes, there are provisions for early redemption and for early payback. It's a non-call, non-put 3. So by year 3, we could actually call the convert and redeem the bonds.

But the actual intention is to let them convert because we have not diluted since 2021. We're very calibrated in the way we plan dilution. So investors can start converting after month 12. And we believe that given where the shares were, where the shares are, the investors perhaps will convert these bonds into equity, which will relieve the balance sheet as we've shown in one of the slides where we simulate leverage ratios with the conversion. Again, investors can start doing that after the first 12 months, and there is a put on year 3 by investors for the bond. The same way we have a call on year 3 for the bond.

Operator: We have one more question from Ailing Chen from Hotwind. Sigma Lithium has been listed on the ASX for more than 2 months, but there appears to be virtually no trading activity or meaningful share price quotation. What is your view on this situation? Why has the Australian listing failed to attract trading activity so far? And what specific steps will the company take to improve liquidity and attract Australian investors? So without active trading, how can the ASX listing achieve its intended purpose?

Ana Cabral Gardner: Absolutely. And the convertible bond note that I was just referring to in the previous answer is the answer to the question. When we listed in Australia, our commitment was to deliver or to execute in the ASX every single issuance the company would do thereafter. So the convertible bond is converted into CDIs, which are the ASX listed shares. So we do believe that when conversion takes place, initially beginning 12 months from now, that ticker, that CDI security will begin to have quite significant liquidity resulting from the converted shares of the bond. Again, the dilution was approximately 14%.

So there's going to be a number of shares that when and if the bond is converted, will flow into the ASX market, hopefully beginning the trading activity you referred to. We're doing our part to act on that listing in order to foster the liquidity and the trading and the note was a demonstration of it. Our first instrument issued was already in Australia.

Operator: The next question comes from Katie Lachapelle from Canaccord Genuity. I want to clarify your comments regarding debt. Is the plan to repay the Synergy debt before year-end instead of in 2027, but then also bring the additional debt?

Ana Cabral Gardner: Katie, well, thanks for the question. Good to see you. Yes, that's exactly the plan. We decided to do the conversion because the refinancing of the debt saves us quite a lot of cash. With the debt reset and the interest rate increases of SOFR, that debt would end up almost in 14% following the reset in December. So our decision is to pay the debt immediately -- immediately after the issuance of the convertible bond closing. We'll pay the debt immediately after the convertible bond closes, which is imminent. So essentially, Synergy will be completely repaid and removed from our balance sheet. And therefore, the balance sheet becomes unencumbered because Synergy is a secured creditor.

The plan going forward, as we've mentioned a few times, is to releverage the balance sheet for the growth strategy. And that will be done with what we call adequate type financing. In other words, as we bring in more debt for growth, we plan to bring in long-term low-cost debt along the same lines of the BNDES debt that we have. So most likely, once we begin this new stage of growth in 2027, we will bring -- we will unlock that credit line in order to tap from it to deliver the growth.

Operator: We have one more question for Katie. Hi Ana, can you provide more specific time lines around the planned growth at Phase 2? When will we open the mine? When you plan to construction commence? Or procurement for the Phase 2 plan components?

Ana Cabral Gardner: Yes. We plan to start opening Mine 2 shortly, very shortly. Most likely, it will be first quarter of next year or later this quarter. Now that will be the foundation of planning for the second plant. We have initiated the construction of the second plant in December 2024. We used quite a lot of our liquidity on it. We continued throughout the first quarter of '25. So what's remaining is procuring for equipment. We've had a procurement sheet, and we estimated based on that procurement sheet updated that there's approximately USD 80 million left of equipment to be ordered. We do not plan to do it now.

We do plan to do it most likely early in the year of 2027. There's a transition of governments here, both in the state and in some of the key positions in federal government. So once all of them are installed in the posts in their positions, we then will proceed on recommencing Mine 2 and Plant 2.

Operator: Next question comes from Rock Hoffman from JPMorgan. First, can you speak to the market dynamics around lithium tailings right now given lower lithium pricing dynamics? It is still a liquid market and would it be possible to sell the full 15,000 tons in the fourth quarter? Or will this material [indiscernible] need to be reprocessed to high grade to be sold?

Ana Cabral Gardner: Both things. It is possible to sell it. The lithium tailings market now looks a lot like it did almost a year ago when we made the decision to go and primarize the mine. Ex Works price for that material now hovers between $30 to $50 -- so that's a net profit. I would say, depending on the lithium quantity of the material, you would have a different Ex Works price. What we got on the plant probably will command a higher price of around $50-ish, perhaps even higher. We typically do not sell tailings against a falling lithium price as we've been seeing, observing in the last 2 weeks.

So we'll stay put and wait further into contract season to make a decision about the tailings. Even though ironically, this is when we get the most amount of offers because that product is very profitable for the client. Essentially, the client just transports it out and throws it into a flotation plant, converting it into very high-grade lithium concentrate. And an example is what's happening with a lot of the African content, which comes out in similar format and becomes very profitable on a fully integrated basis for the battery makers.

Some of these producers being able to live with numbers as low as the equivalent of $500 a ton, which for us, if you convert it back into the lithium content of the tailings benchmarks to approximately USD 30 to USD 50. So it triangulates well with lithium coming out of Nigeria, for example.

Operator: The second question from Rock Hoffman from JPMorgan is, how should we think about your offtake strategy after the main offtake is completed in a few months? Any discussions with partners for additional offtakes or prepayments agreement?

Ana Cabral Gardner: We do have a number of discussions with several partners because we're one of the few large producers with uncommitted material into 2027. We typically strike our offtakes on an annual basis. We strike contracts on an annual basis, and we are considering doing a multiyear offtake agreement into the 2027 year. But typically, for us, we've been achieving very successful commercial results by selling the material on maximum what we call a quarterly contract. For instance, the previous quarter of the third quarter, we achieved a $1,485 realized price, which was very robust if you were to take into account the falling lithium price environment. And we have been over the peers when it comes to achieved realized prices.

Why is that? As we're not hostages to an offtake, we don't price our products on formula. We use the market quote straight out of Shanghai Metals Market for concentrate, which essentially provides a more beneficial financial condition. But we are considering to do a multiyear offtake into 2027, but it's not something necessarily we have to do. We can perfectly survive continuing to do what we always do with selling material on a 1-year basis.

Operator: I'm returning to our CEO, Ana Cabral, for her final remarks.

Ana Cabral Gardner: Felipe and I and the entire Sigma team would like to thank you for your support throughout this quarter. We are very proud of how we came out of the third quarter into the fourth quarter. We came out stronger with tremendous visibility into our business, visibility such that the new governor of Minas Gerais has announced that he's going to take office from our region. So in January, he's actually going to become governor in our region in Vale do Jequitinhonha, which fills us with tremendous pride because we were able to shed the light in the transformational shared prosperity work we have been doing there for almost a decade.

And that has culminated in Sigma becoming this key company in the Western and Eastern global supply chains, delivering large scale, low cost and traceability. Going forward, that decision by the newly elected government has filled us with enthusiasm to full on continue on our growth strategy. And again, starting bottom up because the mine is what brings the most amount of jobs. And as a result, we plan to bring in another 25,000 people into the prosperity fold of Sigma. So working in an endeavor such as this is a partnership between the public powers, between society and between the company.

And as a good citizen company, we're really looking forward to contributing to lift the people of Vale do Jequitinhonha. And for that, I want to thank all of our stakeholders and our shareholders for being with us on this journey.

Operator: The third quarter of 2026 conference call of Sigma Lithium has concluded. For further information, please visit the company's website at www.sigmalithiumresources.com. You can disconnect now.

#3116. 4 new Google Maps features to try on your next holiday road trip

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Tech > Services & Software > Operating Systems > Mobile OS > Android

Google's Ask Maps features start rolling out today on Android and iOS. Here's what they can do for you now.

Even as gas prices dampen some travel plans, you’ll still have plenty of company on the roads this holiday season. AAA predicts that 73 million Americans will travel by car for Thanksgiving between Nov. 24 and Nov. 30. Google Maps is ready to accompany travelers on their journeys with four new features just in time for holiday travel near and far.

In a press release, Google said it’s rolling out four new Ask Maps features that make it easy to create itineraries, find available appointments, and search your saved lists. Here’s what to know about the latest features coming to Google Maps.

Google has made it easy to build step-by-step itineraries and get real-time route details when you pull up directions. You can use Ask Maps to plan simple tasks, like a day of holiday shopping, or more complex plans, like a multi-day road trip with stops along the way.

Also: I tested Google Maps vs. Waze to find the best navigation app

You can get a day-by-day schedule with tips and numbered map pins for each stop, which makes it easy to visualize your plan. You can also share your itinerary with friends and family, or export it to Google Docs. It’s like being your own trip planner without outsourcing the work to a travel agent. To access your itinerary, ask Maps to pull it up, or look for the “itinerary” badge in your chat history. This way, you can see real-time details like live traffic conditions, whether a place is open, and more.

Maps can help you stay ahead. You can now pull up directions with helpful tips before you go, tailored to your route and plan. These include tips on where to park or charge your car, as well as real-time updates on conditions such as weather, potential delays, tolls, and more.

We’re heading into the most wonderful (and busiest) time of year for travel and shopping, and Google wants to reduce your stress. Thanks to new agentic capabilities, you can have Ask Maps find beauty, pet care, auto, and home repair appointments online and call local businesses for you. Ask, “Find a 4 p.m. hair appointment near me,” and Ask Maps will show you open slots at nearby businesses so you can book and go. It’s that easy.

If you’re playing host for the holidays, Google will help you show off all your town’s favorite spots. Now you can use Ask Maps to find saved places on your lists. Ask things like, “Which spots saved in my lists have availability for 6 people in the next half-hour?” Ask Maps scans across your lists and checks live availability so you can pick a place and just go.

Also: I’m an Apple Maps fan, but I switch to Google Maps for these 3 tasks

Updates begin rolling out today on Android and iOS, and Ask Maps is also expanding to 30 countries across Europe, including Spain, Germany, and the UK. Ask Maps will now be available in more than 200 countries and territories. Travel itineraries and list search will be available everywhere Ask Maps is offered, while route tips and appointment locating will first launch in the US, with more regions to follow soon, according to Google.

#3115. Six new Aqara smart lights with Apple Home support and ‘spatial intelligence’

Aqara has announced the global launch of six new smart lighting products with full Apple Home support and what the company describes as “spatial intelligence.”

The new lineup includes a vertical floor lamp with 18 individually addressable lighting zones, and a new LED strip offering seamless color gradients, dynamic flowing effects, and music synchronization …

All of the new products are Matter compatible, allowing them to fully integrate with Apple Home, in addition to supporting the full range of competing ecosystems: Amazon Alexa, Google Home, Samsung SmartThings, Home Assistant, and Homey.

With a compatible sensor like the FP400, all of the new products support spatial intelligence.

This enables automation to respond not only to whether someone is present, but also to exactly where people are within a space and how they move through it. For example, the ambient lights can turn on and off based on your movement from the couch to the dining room table.

Its intelligent AI sensing algorithm drastically improves reliability by reducing false triggers caused by environmental factors like pets, airflow, and robotic vacuums. A built-in ambient light sensor also helps trigger smart home scenes based on both human activity and lighting conditions.

You might initially struggle to spot the new products in the company’s new releases section on its Amazon store. That’s because instead of each having its own section, you need to click or tap on the product in the top image.

Pricing ranges from $24 for new light bulbs through to $320 for the 100-foot-long permanent outdoor rope lights. You can find all the new products here.

#3114. The Simple Trick That Keeps Poached Eggs Perfectly Intact

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

Avoid eggs that fall apart in the pot when you use this genius egg-poaching hack.

Poaching eggs takes practice, but even the gentlest drop into a simmering (never rolling) pot of water can yield sloppy results. It turns out the reason your poached eggs look less like the neat, tidy protein puff you see on food magazine covers and more like a Jackson Pollock has to do with the egg’s structure, not your kitchen skills.

One simple, no-fuss step is all that stands between you and perfect poached eggs, according to a bona fide egg expert I spoke with—and then validated with my not-so-scientific at-home test.

Lisa Steele is a fifth-generation chicken keeper and author of Fresh Eggs Daily and In Season: 125+ Sweet and Savory Recipes Celebrating Simple, Fresh Ingredients. She talked me through the single, foolproof step that makes stovetop egg poaching dead simple.

Picture it: a pot full of water, maybe with a dash of distilled vinegar, at the gentlest simmer so you don’t subject your delicate egg to a tornado of activity when you submerge it. You painstakingly crack the egg into a shallow bowl first and carefully slip it into the pot. Regardless of your good intentions, the egg then clouds the water and turns all wispy, like some sort of blond dementor.

You haven’t done anything wrong here; you’ve just failed to understand an egg’s basic structure. “There are actually two components of the egg white, or albumen,” Steele explains. “There’s the thicker part of the white which encases the yolk, and then there’s a separate, thinner layer of egg white around that. It’s the thinner part of the egg white that will spread and turn wispy when you drop an egg into the water.”

The thing is, you can easily get rid of the thin, watery white part of your egg using one simple tool you’ve probably got in a drawer somewhere and about a minute of your time. Set a small mesh strainer over a cup or bowl, crack the egg into it, and wait.

“Straining an egg removes the thinner whites that likely won’t adhere to the rest of the egg and result in shaggy, wispy threads,” Steele says. “It won’t affect the flavor outcome of your poached egg, but it is purely for appearance’s sake.” (And potentially your sanity’s or sense of accomplishment’s sake, I might add.)

While the egg’s flavor stays unchanged, for Benedict lovers, straining the egg first slightly improves the white-to-yolk ratio in the poached result and makes the texture more consistent, while also creating a tidy, photogenic package.

Once your raw egg is in the strainer, you may notice nothing happens right away, and you may feel the urge to move the egg around a bit to get things going. But don’t zhush, which threatens to scramble the egg. Simply wait for gravity to do its thing; it takes about a minute. It’s akin to what happens when separating whites from yolks, except here you’re separating whites from whites.

“Let the thin part of the egg white drip down into the bowl,” Steele says, “then gently slide the egg into the simmering water.” The strainer can also serve as a handy vessel for transferring the egg, especially if you’re making only one. If you’re doing multiple eggs and don’t want to risk cooking any remaining white onto the mesh by submerging it, place the strained egg in a small, shallow bowl as usual before easing it into the water. Without the thin, watery white part, you’ll notice a discernible textural difference in the egg even when raw.

The straining step alone can almost completely change your poached egg game in an instant, but for the best results, follow the best poaching protocol. You don’t want a full pot of water at a rolling boil like you would for pasta. “Fill a pot or saucepan with a few inches of water and bring to a boil, then turn the heat down to low so the water is just barely simmering with small bubbles floating to the surface,” Steele advises.

Creating a little whirlpool will further help your remaining egg white stay snug. “Using a wooden spoon or silicone spatula, swirl the water, then gently slide the egg into the center of the whirlpool as you keep swirling for another few seconds around the egg until the egg white turns milky and starts to set up around the yolk,” Steele says. “At this point, you can push the egg to one side, add another egg into the center and repeat the process.”

A soft-poached egg takes about three minutes, and because you’ve removed the watery part of the egg white, you’ll get a nice firm structure to hold the still-runny yolk — the poached egg ideal.

Since poaching is a delicate process, no matter your new straining habit and how strictly you follow the recommended procedure, “using the freshest eggs possible is very important when you are poaching because the egg white gets even more thin and watery as the egg ages,” Steele says. “The membrane holding the yolk together also weakens, making the yolk more susceptible to breaking.” So if you don’t have them on hand already, get yourself a strainer and some fresh eggs and put this newfound tidbit to the personal test.

Cooking bacon in the oven is a great way to make a large batch, but the air fryer method might be even better — and it’s definitely faster. Here are nine more cooking hacks that save time and energy.

#3112. The Android camera app that doesn’t overprocess adds new color grading sets, expands to iPhone

VWFNDR + MBL, an Android camera app that doesn’t overprocess and delivers high-quality DNG (RAW) files, is getting a 2.0 release with improved color grading and an expansion to the iPhone.

VWFNDR + MBL launched on Android in May 2026 with a few points that stood out. A unique UI that adapts to the shot, minimal processing for a natural look, and support for DNG files at a level that only Google’s Pixel Camera app can truly compete with.

The app has been downloaded over 300,000 times since then, and is now getting a pretty substantial update.

On Android, this comes in the form of new color grading profiles built into the app. “NATURAL,” “NIHON,” or “B+W.” The app still saves an unprocessed DNG alongside the JPG and the grading adapts across the frame rather than having a fixed result, keeping highlights and shadows in place.

Colour grades: MBL still records unprocessed Bayer RAW DNG, and the JPG it renders alongside now uses one of three grades: NATURAL, NIHON, or B+W. Grading happens on VWFNDR’s own spatial engine. Instead of applying a fixed LUT, it adapts across the frame, much like a raw editor, so highlights and shadows keep their detail. The DNG stays untouched.

The rest of VWFNDR + MBL 2.0 takes place off of Android.

In a rare case of the tables turning, MBL was released first on Android, and only on Android for the first several months. But VWFNDR is now bringing the app to iPhone with support for variable aperture on iPhone 18 Pro and Content Credentials, Apple’s version of the C2PA standard that’s meant to prove a photo is real and not AI-generated.

#3110. Alphabet vs. Apple: Which Warren Buffett Stock Is the Better Buy?

Both are major positions in the Berkshire Hathaway portfolio.

By Adria Cimino – Nov 18, 2026 at 6:25PM EST

Warren Buffett is known for selecting quality stocks and holding on to them for many years. And he's proven that this strategy works: For 60 years as chief executive officer at Berkshire Hathaway, Buffett helped deliver market-beating returns. Buffett retired at the beginning of this year, but he remains involved at Berkshire Hathaway and now holds the title of chairman emeritus.

Greg Abel, who took over from Buffett as CEO, has maintained the investing giant's principles and continues to hold many Buffett favorites. Two in particular remain among the company's top holdings: Apple (AAPL +0.15%) and Alphabet (GOOG +0.58%) (GOOGL +0.80%), in the No. 1 and No. 4 positions, respectively.

Which of these Warren Buffett stocks is the better buy today? Let's find out.

Warren Buffett. Image source: Getty Images.

This year marks a 10-year anniversary for Apple and Berkshire Hathaway: Buffett initially bought Apple shares in 2016. And over the years, it's become a cherished position, with Buffett on multiple occasions praising Tim Cook, who held the CEO role until September of this year.

Cook, who recently retired, helped the company's market value soar 1,000% to $4 trillion and revenue almost quadruple to $416 billion in the 2025 fiscal year. Now, with John Ternus at the helm, there's reason to be optimistic about more growth ahead. Ternus, formerly the company's senior vice president of hardware engineering, has the product experience and knowledge to lead Apple through new waves of innovation. Products are Apple's strength, with the iPhone the global smartphone leader, so a product focus is key for future growth.

Apple stock has climbed more than that of fellow tech giants this year, as it isn't as heavily linked to artificial intelligence (AI) -- and therefore is less sensitive to AI-related risks. Though Apple stock isn't cheap, it still could have room to run.

Buffett opened a position in Alphabet last year, and Abel added to it this year, showing clear commitment to this Buffett selection. Alphabet climbed earlier this year but has been under pressure in recent times, along with other tech giants that are investing heavily in AI. Some investors worry that these players are overspending and that the revenue opportunity will be disappointing.

Still, Alphabet's Google Cloud business hasn't faltered; in fact, that unit's revenue has been soaring amid strong demand for its AI products and services. In the recent quarter, Google Cloud revenue jumped 103% to $30 billion. The company has also begun selling its own chips, known as TPUs, to certain customers for use in their data centers. Though this is a small source of revenue right now, it could grow in time.

Meanwhile, Google's search business continues to hold 90% of the search market worldwide, and this has been its ticket to enormous revenue year after year. This is through advertising, with advertisers eager to place ads across the platform to reach potential customers. In the recent quarter, Google ads brought in $82 billion in revenue for the company.

Alphabet stock today looks cheap, particularly compared with that of Apple.

There's a clear reason for this, however, and this goes back to the point I made above: Some investors are turning away from AI big spenders. But this opens up an opportunity to buy Alphabet at a fantastic price.

This depends on your investment style and priorities. From a valuation perspective, Alphabet clearly stands out. Today, this tech giant is a great deal for growth investors looking for a bargain. Though current market sentiment may continue to weigh on Alphabet stock, this doesn't change the company's long-term story.

Alphabet's search business remains solid, and the company's cloud business is well-established and growing -- and doesn't rely uniquely on AI. So investors may benefit if they buy now and hold on as the storm passes.

However, Apple, less linked to AI spending and a long-term Buffett favorite, may be a better buy for the cautious investor. Though the stock has climbed, the release of new products just recently could boost revenue and lead to more gains ahead.

#3109. The World Didn’t End on Nov. 17, but Some Tech Chaos Did Go Down

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

Despite hacking causing some problems for websites, the dire predictions for widespread Nov. 17 catastrophe appeared not to have come true. An emergency alert did air on radio and TV.

As global conspiracy theories go, this was a juicy one.

On Tuesday, Nov. 17, at around 2:20 p.m. ET, the Federal Emergency Management Agency and the Federal Communications Commission conducted a test of the Emergency Alert System. That’s when all hell was supposed to break loose. At least, that’s what you might have believed if you only relied on social media.

The good news: The world didn’t break at that time despite fears. The bad news: Some troubling activity did, in fact, happen, even if it may have been unrelated or the result of opportunistic hackers taking advantage of the anxiety. Attackers targeted hundreds of websites with malware seeking to hijack data from credit card transactions, Apple software or cryptocurrency transactions. Sites affected included CNN, IKEA, Fox News and Zoom.

Apple and Google also experienced issues on Tuesday, but it’s unclear if those are related to the hacking that affected websites. Apple’s System Status page reported outages of App Store, Apple Music and iCloud services among others, while some Google users reported issues with their email.

Coming just days after an abrupt and disruptive government-ordered shutdown of air travel in the US and technical issues that caused an unwelcome outage of widely used Microsoft workplace software, the hacking and the government’s alert test happened in an atmosphere of heightened anxiety.

Videos across Facebook, Instagram and TikTok floated the theory that this emergency test signals a catastrophe was coming, potentially stemming from a cyberattack or a digital disruption that could knock out electricity, internet and other services. Many scrambled to buy emergency supplies, pointing to the need for a 90-day stockpile of food, water, cash and essential medicines in case hackers wipe out bank accounts and shut down the web.

Similar rumors spread globally, as the governments of France, the UK and Canada have put renewed attention on the importance of households being able to survive a potential weather-related crisis or technological disaster.

How extreme did the conspiracy theories get? Some cited a 2023 Simpsons episode as proof, which referenced a massive Nov. 17 blackout in Lisa’s future, even though it didn’t mention a year.

For Gen Xers and Boomers, this panic could feel familiar. Leading up to the year 2000, there were fears that a potential computer-related disaster, known as Y2K, would cause widespread chaos and disruption, based on the belief that older digital systems couldn’t handle the calendar change. The new year ended with only minor glitches, thanks to a significant global effort to update computer systems to avoid the bug.

Before we delve into the suspicions, let’s start with a bit of debunking: CNET spoke with multiple experts in disaster preparedness and cyberattacks, who all cautioned against letting our guard down, no matter what the date. But remember that no federal agency or institution has mentioned a blackout.

Richard Mariano, a protective intelligence expert at Kronus Intelligence, who spent nearly three decades with the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives, said that people share all sorts of things that get picked up and go viral. “Then it creates panic where panic is not necessary,” he said.

Mariano said too many people are spreading fear rather than seeking the truth. “On every one of these social media posts that is suspect or has some form of conspiratorial edge to them: source it, source it, source it.”

The Emergency Alert System message scheduled for Nov. 17 was similar to the public tests Americans have experienced since 1963, (PDF) when the Emergency Broadcast System replaced an older radio-based warning system called CONELRAD. In 1997, the Emergency Broadcast System was replaced by the EAS, part of FEMA’s Integrated Public Alert and Warning System, which broadcasts emergency alerts to any wireless device in the country, including phones, radios and televisions. The system was designed for the president to communicate with US households within 10 minutes of a national emergency.

The Nov. 17 test consisted of a nationwide EAS message issued by FEMA, noting that no public action is required. The test included standard alert tones to support accessibility for those who are deaf or hard of hearing and lasted about a minute. This time around, wireless emergency alerts were not triggered on mobile phones. After the alert, programming resumed as normal on TV, radio and other broadcast channels.

Many equate the emergency system with threats of nuclear war, but it could also be used to alert people to a major weather event, a national cyberattack or even AMBER alerts at the local level (without a presidential message). So it’s natural there might be some anxiety.

“With this event simulating an activation of an emergency notification system, it would be a logical next step to worry about what happens if something bad happens during that test,” said Robby Winchester, chief global professional services officer at SpecterOps, a Virginia-based security company,

But, all in all, these system tests are routine. Local stations conduct a weekly test, and federal law requires a nationwide EAS test every three years. In addition to helping people get used to responding to alerts, the tests also allow the government to identify potential technical or operational issues it needs to fix before an actual emergency alert.

Representatives from the FCC and FEMA did not respond to a request for comment.

Another factor that helped spark conspiracy theories was a Pentagon order requiring military bases to stock enough supplies for 90 days without outside support. Dubbed “Fortress America,” the initiative memo (PDF) was released in late September but got more attention as the November date approached.

The timing of that memo coincided with the UK launching a campaign on Oct. 22 called Be Ready, urging citizens to keep enough supplies (PDF) such as water, food, medical kits and pet products to last at least three days. Other countries, including Japan, Sweden and about a dozen more, are also urging citizens to prepare for emergencies.

Still, the blackout rumor isn’t solely driven by government communications. Heightened global instability over the past few months has also played a major role. Just in the last month, the Federal Aviation Administration called a nationwide ground stop on all departing flights; a major Microsoft Outlook outage kept millions of people from working; PHP vulnerabilities exposed websites to hacking; and cyberattacks have targeted supermarket fridges and freezers across Europe.

On the financial side, Nvidia’s CEO scandal led to a stock plunge and fears of an AI bust, while Paraguay just experienced a major digital bank collapse that froze millions of accounts. The ongoing wars in Iran and Ukraine have sparked national security concerns, and floods in Nepal and fires in Indonesia demonstrate the increased dangers of climate change.

Though there’s never been a nationwide power outage in the US (several regional outages have been triggered by overloaded lines and software bugs), The New York Times reports that there’s still no comprehensive plan for what to do if the country goes completely dark.

All the online chatter surrounding Nov. 17 raised concerns that warnings of a potential cyberattack might inadvertently trigger one.

Winchester said that even though there’s no specific information indicating an imminent crisis, “it is common for attackers to use current events of all types to help with achieving successful attacks.” The upside? If people are being spurred by government notices and their anxiety over global instability to prepare emergency supplies, it could actually help in the event of a real threat or disaster.

Regardless of whether you bought into the Nov. 17 conspiracy theories, it doesn’t hurt to have some supplies on hand, which could be useful in the event of a digital disruption or weather event, even if it doesn’t involve nuclear weapons or hackers.

“We live in a world where there are many threats to our communities, our families and ourselves,” said Philip Farina, chief advisor for Risky Business and a federal law enforcement veteran. “Understanding the basics of self-reliance is important. Even preparing for a residential fire, which is very common, can help to save lives and protect us better.”

You don’t need to buy enough for 90 days off the grid (and most of us can’t afford that), but it’s recommended that families have at least three days’ worth of food and supplies. Some of the basics listed on Ready.gov’s Build a Kit page include:

While warnings from governments can spark panic and distrust, they can be beneficial at a time when we’re so reliant on the internet and cell service, which can be easily disrupted. Mariano said it’s worth being prepared in the “old-fashioned ways.”

#3107. iPhone Duo 2 prototypes suggest Face ID, Action Button, other potential 2027 features

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

With manufacturing deadlines looming, it's unclear which of several feature upgrades may have to wait until the foldable's third generation.

Although the iPhone Duo was released just this fall, Apple is finalizing the foldable’s second generation. According to a Bloomberg report, Apple has already created prototypes for the second iPhone Duo, codenamed V78, and some include a sought-after feature: Face ID.

Apple reportedly wants to bring Face ID to the foldable, potentially integrating it into the outer display. However, Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman notes that Apple appears to be running out of time to finalize its plans for the Duo ahead of a fall 2027 launch.

Also: iPhone Duo review: Hard to recommend, even harder to put down

iPhone launch events typically take place in early September, when Apple releases its new smartphone lineups. To have the iPhones ready for sale on the heels of their announcement, Apple must manufacture the new models well before the launch event.

Because of this timeline concern, Face ID isn’t guaranteed for the iPhone Duo 2, though it could come to a third generation instead.

Other planned uogrades — including an Action Button, a telephoto camera, and a thinner, lighter construction — are also noted in the report.

Apple reportedly wants to add an Action Button, the customizable button that performs an action when pressed. The iPhone Duo 2 may combine the Action Button and the Camera Control buttons into a single button, providing a useful physical shortcut instead of adding a new button.

The report indicates that many users don’t use the camera control button as often as Apple expected. Combining the camera and action buttons gives Apple the real estate necessary to add both options in an already constrained space.

Apple also wants to incorporate a telephoto camera into the iPhone Duo, though this is likely to happen in one of the next couple of generations. A telephoto camera would give users greater flexibility to zoom in and capture clear photos of distant objects, which would be an upgrade to the Duo’s photography features.

Technically, equipping the Duo with a telephoto camera is feasible, but the biggest obstacle is space constraints. A telephoto camera needs more room than a wide-angle one, since it requires additional optical elements to magnify distant objects.

Apple already uses a tetraprism design in its Pro iPhones, which allows a longer optical path without too much physical depth.

Apple also wants to reduce the weight and thickness of the iPhone Duo, which is legitimately clunky and cumbersome. To do this, Apple needs to balance the large internal and outer displays, battery capacity, camera array, and the hinge mechanism.

Also: The iPhone Action Button you’re hardly using has a superpower

For many users, reducing the weight and thickness of a passport-sized foldable could matter more in buying decisions than adding another button or camera.

Gurman’s latest report doesn’t mention any planned changes for the iPhone Duo’s hinge mechanism, even after concerns with the first generation’s durability. With manufacturing deadlines fast approaching, however, it’s unlikely that Apple will be able to make changes to the Duo 2 based on consumer feedback. More than likely, these changes would come with the third-generation model.

CNET tested the iPhone Duo’s hinge mechanism and found that, after around 440,000 cycles, the hinge stopped opening flat on its own. Loosening and other signs of wear were evident after 390,000 folds.

Also: The best iPhone Duo cases: Expert recommended

Given the thinner, lighter construction of a future Duo model, one could assume that changes to the hinge and the foldable’s internal structure are imminent, but this has not been confirmed.

Because Apple will not have enough time to gather feedback on the iPhone Duo before the manufacturing deadlines for the iPhone Duo 2, I don’t expect the second-generation iPhone Duo to be significantly different from its predecessor. We do expect a thinner iPhone Duo 2 and a way to incorporate the Action and Camera buttons.

#3105. Cyberattack Targets iPhones, Crypto of Visitors to Major Websites

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

Tech > Services & Software > Cybersecurity

Hackers tried to inject malware for people going to Ikea, CNN, Zoom and other popular sites.

If you visited Ikea, CNN, Zoom or several other popular websites on Monday, it might be wise to update your iPhone or iPad immediately. Cybercriminals tried to infect iPhones and steal cryptocurrency from people who went to those sites, Reuters reports.

The compromised websites include Zoom, BBC, CNN, Salesforce, GitLab, Ikea, HSBC, Equifax, Air France-KLM, Ledger and Peacock, according to cybersecurity researcher Scott Helme and his platform Report URI. Helme said bad actors used Optimizely, a website optimization company, in an attempt to serve up JavaScript malware to people visiting sites from 178 organizations.

Ikea said it was investigating to see if any customers or digital services had been impacted. Zoom said it disabled Optimizely across its production environments and had not identified any effect on customer data. Equifax also has stopped using Optimizely and said it has not identified any compromise to systems or data.

Helme told CNET that “most people who simply read a page are at low risk,” but there are other actions you should take if you did more than that. He said if you entered debit or credit card details on any of the affected sites (the full list is here), check transactions and statements and maybe even get a replacement card.

If you copied and pasted a crypto wallet address on a site, make sure the funds went to the intended recipient, Helme suggested. Also, log out of all sessions on the affected websites and change your password. Finally, update to the latest iOS and restart the device if you use an iPhone or iPad running iOS 18.6 or earlier.

Optimizely said that the criminal “exploited a vulnerability in Experimentation” — the website testing system that clients use — to add the malicious JavaScript. The company said it had fixed the vulnerability, removed the bad code and “taken steps to secure affected user accounts.”

Reuters reported that Salesforce, Equifax and HSBC said their sites had not been compromised by the incident. Reuters also said it could not determine how much theft had occurred in the attack.

Report URI said that more than $7,000 in crypto was stolen within several hours of the attack’s start.

Optimizely is a platform used by many websites to manage content, test new website designs and tailor product recommendations to various target audiences. Customers load JavaScript snippets, which include Optimizely code and customer experiments, onto their websites to optimize site performance.

The snippets also contain a Project JavaScript field, which consists of code written by customers. But on Monday, the cybercriminal injected malicious code into that Project JavaScript field. Because the rest of the snippet was untouched, the files were still served from a host that every affected site already trusted.

The cost of cybercrime is forecast to reach $12.2 trillion by 2031, according to one estimate, an annual increase of 2.5% from 2026. That amount includes “stolen funds, fraud, productivity loss, intellectual property theft, post-attack remediation, regulatory fines and reputational harm.”

The Optimizely incident, dubbed the OptimJack attack, was the latest in a series of internet incidents around the globe. On Thursday, Microsoft’s Outlook email system went down, and the FAA grounded all planes on Friday. Microsoft blamed a software bug from July, and the FAA blamed a router.

Then, on Monday, Chase reported service disruptions and transaction delays, as did some Apple services on Tuesday.

None of these incidents were connected, Helme told CNET.

#3103. 5 ways AI will change how you defend your business in 2027

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Security leaders reveal the future consequences of AI outpacing human defenders.

At the beginning of the year, few organizations were utilizing large language models (LLMs) and AI agents in their cybersecurity workflows, including for discovering and patching vulnerabilities. According to Google, this is now happening at scale.

Also: Rogue AI incidents hit ‘tens of thousands’: Can businesses trust these tools?

The capabilities of agentic AI are fast outstripping the speed and scale at which traditional security operations centers (SOCs) can operate. Like it or not, AI has an integral role in the new reality — for the defenders and threat actors.

Speed and scale are the main reasons enterprises consider adopting AI in SOCs and for security more broadly, and these factors underpin Google’s new security forecast for 2027 — Cloud CISO Perspectives. However, without the right precautions, AI security adopters could inadvertently increase their attack surface rather than shrink it.

With this in mind, these are five ways AI will change the security industry over the next year and what CISOs need to consider going into 2027.

Alert fatigue is well-known across SOC teams. Alert after alert needs to be trawled through; many are irrelevant or false positives, tying up skilled staff with the mundane, tedious, time-consuming task of triaging them.

Now that autonomous, AI-driven threats can probe a network, gain entry, and move laterally across it in minutes, chasing threat data and security alerts from multiple systems logged days or weeks ago can’t help a business mitigate them — and certainly not at the speed of the threat.

According to Google’s forecast, AI will mean the alert queue quietly disappears. Ramya Chitrakar, VP of engineering at Google Cloud Security, believes that “2027 is the year analysts stop chasing alerts and start shaping outcomes.”

Also: AI is both a cyber weapon and a massive target

How? CISOs must change the alert model itself. Instead of human defenders triaging alerts at the start of a cybersecurity incident, the alert becomes final output, with autonomous agents handling “data enrichment, correlation, and triage automatically, surfacing a verified conclusion rather than a raw ticket,” according to Google.

This means cybersecurity experts can oversee alert handling and verify automated actions, potentially freeing them to focus on other tasks.

Custom agentic AI is often designed — or at least intended — to work autonomously, with human oversight. However, having thousands of individual agents working across multiple environments can create high-value entry points into corporate networks that cyberattackers target.

We need to think of agentic AI as more than a tool: each one needs its own identity, like a human employee, to operate within a zero-trust architecture, retain control, and reduce the risk of compromise.

Also: Your enterprise AI access can be sold for pennies – beware ‘LLM Mixers’

However, Heather Adkins, VP of security engineering at Google, thinks this needs to go further and suggests the zero-trust concept shouldn’t stop at the network layer. Instead, Adkins believes it needs to reach the transaction layer.

A paper trail for each agent needs to be established, which is impossible to handle manually, and even within a zero-trust framework, AI agents could be given too much scope. Instead, implement verification for each transaction and for every authorization, and assign each AI agent its own least-privilege set of credentials that can be revoked if there is a security incident or the agent is no longer required.

“When backed by real-time autonomous reasoning, we can dynamically allow a transaction on Tuesday and block the exact same request on Wednesday if conditions look anomalous,” the report notes.

AI is being used to speed up the development and deployment of new software, and in 2027, security will have to become a continuous system embedded in the software delivery pipeline, according to Google.

Threat actors have carried out software supply chain attacks over the years, one of the most notable being the SolarWinds incident of 2020. Sandra Joyce, VP of Google Threat Intelligence, says cybercriminals are now poisoning everything from open-source code to software libraries, which AI coding assistants often pull automatically into codebases.

Also: How AI security failures are endangering your supply chain

Bug-fix tickets that take days to respond to and security appearing at the end of a software development cycle no longer work. Instead, writing and securing code must happen simultaneously, with the help of agentic AI, so speed doesn’t compromise security.

“It’s also crucial that we link live production environments directly back to source code so that defenders can trace a real-world exposure to the exact line of code, validate whether it is genuinely exploitable, and deliver a pre-tested fix at machine speed without breaking production,” Google added.

As organizations rush to implement AI into their applications and services to appear “AI-first,” innovative, and modern, security may be ignored or treated as an afterthought.

As a result, we may face a new, broader attack surface than we realize, as AI introduces new security issues, including software vulnerabilities, misconfiguration, bypasses, and indirect prompt injection attacks. Now that AI is also in the hands of all cyberattackers — from script kiddies to state-sponsored groups — auditing corporate networks and infrastructure is crucial.

Also: Who’s responsible for catching rogue AI agents? You are

Penetration testing and red team exercises now need to cover agentic AI. This wasn’t in scope for many red teams only a few years ago, but now that businesses have run with the idea of implementing AI in their workflows, processes, and products, organizations need to identify and fix security issues introduced by AI before threat actors take advantage of them.

CISOs should task pen testers with auditing before an autonomous workflow hits production, then combine the results with threat intelligence to ensure defenders have the information they need to bolster network defenses and harden classifiers against new and novel attacks.

The final significant trend we are likely to see in 2027 is tackling agent sprawl to create coordinated teams of AI agents that can rapidly handle security tasks at scale.

Single AI agents given general instructions won’t cut it when AI-assisted attackers can compromise endpoint devices, enter networks, move laterally, or start stealing data in a far shorter timeframe than before. Instead, CISOs should replace these “generalist” AI agents with specialized, orchestrated teams of AI agents that can meet the demands of defending against AI-driven attacks by employing specialist tooling and skill sets.

Also: AI agent kill switch urged by Okta-led alliance

CISOs also need to ensure that each agent has its own domain training and understanding, memory, and dedicated tools, and can act on its own within set limits, with a central coordinator that knows when to hand a decision to a human. This requires oversight, but in return, organizations will avoid agent sprawl, which the tech giant believes is the next iteration of shadow IT and its associated threats.

#3102. Blackstone Digital Infrastructure: 3 Key Takeaways for Long-Term Investors

Amazon keeps a 25% stake in the joint venture, a structure that ties the tenant's fortunes to the portfolio's performance.

By The Motley Fool Team – Nov 18, 2026 at 6:26PM EST

10 stocks we like better than Blackstone Digital Infrastructure Trust ›

On its third-quarter 2026 earnings call, held on Nov. 16, 2026, Blackstone Digital Infrastructure (BXDC +0.18%) announced a deal to acquire a 75% interest in a $5 billion portfolio of 13 powered shell data centers (facilities where the landlord owns the building and power connection while the tenant supplies equipment) leased to Amazon. The deal would transition the trust from holding cash to generating steady rental income backed by an investment-grade technology titan. For long-term investors, this initial purchase establishes the template for how the company plans to scale its portfolio. Three things management said stand out.

Management committed its initial capital to acquire a 75% majority interest in a $5 billion data center portfolio. Amazon retained the remaining 25% minority stake as a joint venture (a cooperative business partnership) under a triple net lease (an agreement where the tenant pays property taxes, insurance, and maintenance costs), ensuring the technology titan remains aligned with the property's performance.

Powered shells have fewer ongoing landlord responsibilities than turnkey facilities. The transaction delivers a 7% going-in capitalization rate (cap rate, the initial annual rental yield on a property investment), along with 2.75% annual rent increases that protect against inflation.

Hyperscalers (large-scale cloud providers requiring vast computing capacity) face massive infrastructure spending demands to support artificial intelligence. Purchasing existing assets through sale-leaseback transactions (where an owner sells property and immediately leases it back) doubles the company's addressable market (the total market opportunity) to over $2 trillion by 2030.

Data center demand is expanding into power-rich regions such as Indiana and Mississippi, where early positioning offers a distinct advantage. Blackstone's platform scale and sourcing pipeline give the trust access to a wide range of on- and off-market deals.

Management is evaluating an expanding pipeline of upcoming asset deliveries while focusing on disciplined capital allocation and tenant alignment.

#3101. SpaceX Misses Its Double Catch but Still Makes History by Catching the Starship

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

The Super Heavy V3 booster fell into the Gulf of Mexico, where it was later recovered

SpaceX came up short on an ambitious double-catch attempt during Friday’s Launch 15, snagging only one of the two rockets it aimed to recover. The company hoped to capture both the Starship spacecraft and the Super Heavy V3 booster, building on a maneuver it first pulled off with a single booster just over two years ago and has since repeated multiple times.

SpaceX’s Launch 15 lifted off cleanly Friday evening, reaching orbit to deploy 26 Starlink V3 satellites before the stages returned to Earth. Back in Boca Chica, Texas, ground crews aimed to snag the upgraded Super Heavy V3 booster using Mechazilla, SpaceX’s towering launch-and-catch structure. While the company had previously caught its older V1 booster three times, Friday’s flight marked its first attempt to recover the V3 variant.

That recovery attempt fell short. SpaceX is still investigating the cause, though spokesperson Kate Tice noted during Friday’s webcast that the booster “ended its boostback (burn) early due to a low fuel mass alarm.” The premature shutdown forced the Super Heavy V3 to splash down in the Gulf of Mexico, where recovery crews later retrieved it.

Meanwhile, the upper-stage Starship pressed on, deploying its satellites and completing roughly 14 orbits before reentering on Saturday. Nearly 24 hours after liftoff, SpaceX successfully caught the returning spacecraft with Mechazilla.

“Starship navigated its way back to the east coast of Texas, flew a final swoosh maneuver out over the Gulf, and approached the same launch site it had just left 22.5 hours prior,” SpaceX said in a statement. “After breaking through the clouds, three Raptor engines ignited for a landing flip and slow descent into Mechazilla’s waiting arms, which closed to catch Starship for the very first time.”

The initial goal was to catch both the Super Heavy V3 booster and the Starship itself, a feat that SpaceX had not attempted before. It also would’ve been the first time in human history that a space company caught both its booster rocket and the upper stage, which would’ve scored a big win for rocket reusability.

SpaceX was unable to secure the Super Heavy V3 booster, but it was still able to catch the Starship. Despite missing the dual catch, the operation represents a significant engineering milestone, as it is the first time SpaceX has successfully caught a rocket’s upper stage after launch.

SpaceX streamed the flight from its X account and the company’s website. You can watch the entire webcast on X. It lasts approximately 23.5 hours and covers the launch, the Super Heavy V3 crash into the Gulf of Mexico and the eventual catch of the Starship.

Apple is leaning into AI-powered health tools with the launch of its Apple Health AI Usage Study.

Apple is exploring how people use AI for their health, presumably to build its own AI health coach. On Sunday, it launched the Apple Health AI Usage Study, which could contribute to the next AI health experience Apple builds by measuring the quality of AI health responses, comprehension, and everyday health behaviors, according to a press release.

Apple is conducting the study in collaboration with OpenEvidence, a clinical AI platform widely used by healthcare professionals. The study examines the relationship between conversational AI tools, like chatbots, and the people who use them.

“Insights from this study will help advance the broader scientific conversation and ensure that as technology evolves, we continue building trusted tools that genuinely support people wherever they are on their health journey,” Sumbul Desai, M.D., Apple’s vice president of Health and Fitness, said in the press release.

Also: Apple Watch Series 12 review: Finally, the health tracker I’ve been waiting for

Participants are encouraged to share their HealthKit data and query the health app with questions. The study will also explore how AI tools can best prepare patients ahead of clinical visits. Apple will monitor the AI’s clarity and approachability when providing medical information, and each response or recommendation will be linked to peer-reviewed clinical citations. Responses could be unclear or incomplete, which is why Apple is rolling this out as a study to explore a responsibly designed AI health assistant.

Apple often launches studies for features it would like to develop in the future. For example, many of the hearing health features launched on the AirPods were a direct result of the findings from Apple’s Hearing Study.

Also: Athenahealth patients can ask Claude about their medical records now

The AI usage study comes on the heels of the revamped Health app’s debut, which launches officially next month. It also arrives amid a bevy of AI health coaches, popping up alongside companion health devices. Google launched its AI Health Coach in Google Health Premium last year, and Oura launched a proprietary AI model for women trained on medical standards and research from Oura’s in-house team of board-certified clinicians.

A growing number of Americans are relying on AI for medical advice. A recent survey from Pew Research Center found that 34% of US adults have talked with a chatbot for medical advice. As AI proliferates, that percentage will only increase.

“Patients and clinicians are both turning to AI, but the tools they use are being built and tested in separate worlds,” said Robert M. Wachter, M.D., UCSF’s professor and chair of the Department of Medicine, in the press release.

Apple and other tech companies are building for this new health normal, and the AI usage study indicates that Apple isn’t taking the responsibility lightly.

If you’re interested in participating in Apple’s study, it’s open to 200,000 eligible participants age 21 and older in the US. You’ll need a phone with Apple Intelligence enabled (the iPhone 15 Pro or later), running iOS 26 or later. You can download the study app to learn more and enroll.

#3097. Prediction: This Will Be Sandisk’s Stock Price by the End of 2027

Sandisk stock's recent slide isn't justified, and I won't be surprised to see a big rally over the coming year.

By Harsh Chauhan – Nov 18, 2026 at 6:30PM EST

After an incredible rally in the first half of 2026, shares of Sandisk (SNDK -2.64%) have pulled back at an alarming pace in recent months.

The stock has retreated 60% since the beginning of July. Investors have been booking profits in Sandisk stock for various reasons. For instance, the broader semiconductor industry has been under pressure in recent months, as Wall Street is concerned about whether the incredible pace of spending on artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure is sustainable amid rising inflation, which has led the Federal Reserve to increase interest rates.

However, this isn't the only reason why Sandisk stock has taken a beating. Concerns about the state of the NAND flash industry that Sandisk serves have played a central role in the stock's decline. Let's look at the factors impacting Sandisk stock lately and check if it can step on the gas in 2027.

Sandisk manufactures NAND flash storage products, including enterprise solid-state drives (SSDs) that are used in AI data centers. The shortage of traditional hard-disk drives (HDDs) forced hyperscalers and AI companies to turn to SSDs to store huge data sets for training and inference workloads.

The demand for NAND flash storage significantly outpaced supply, creating a major shortage that led to a sharp price spike. Market research firm Gartner estimates that NAND flash prices will rise by 293% in 2026, as demand exceeds supply by 9%. The shortage is expected to persist into 2027, with demand exceeding supply by 5%. As a result, Gartner predicts a 30% increase in NAND flash prices next year.

This slower increase in prices has spooked investors, who now believe that Sandisk's days of hypergrowth could be coming to an end. Meanwhile, TrendForce reports that weak consumer demand for NAND has led to a 20% drop in spot prices in just two weeks. The shortage of data center graphics cards in China has led to a decline in enterprise SSD demand, thereby lowering prices.

These divergent views about the state of the NAND flash market in 2027 have weighed on Sandisk's shares recently. However, it is worth noting that lower spot prices don't necessarily mean that the NAND flash market will enter a downward spiral next year. That's because spot contracts usually involve small lot sizes and reportedly account for only 5% of NAND flash revenue.

Contract prices decide the market's direction, as NAND flash customers like to plan well in advance for their needs. This explains why Sandisk has already sold a large chunk of its NAND flash supply for the next two fiscal years under long-term agreements.

Sandisk management noted on the October earnings call that it has already sold 50% of its supply capacity for fiscal 2027 under long-term contracts. Even better, the company has demand commitments for two-thirds of its fiscal 2028 capacity. Management added that its long-term contract pipeline exceeds its supply capacity through the end of the decade.

So, Sandisk has demand visibility for the long run, which explains why its financial performance in fiscal 2027, which has just begun, is going to be solid.

Sandisk's revenue in the first quarter of fiscal 2027 (which ended Oct. 2) increased by 378% year over year to $11 billion. The company's non-GAAP earnings per share jumped from just $1.22 in the year-ago period to $49.51 in the previous quarter.

Importantly, analysts have become bullish on Sandisk's earnings growth prospects for the next three years.

SNDK EPS Estimates for Current Fiscal Year data by YCharts

Assuming Sandisk's earnings jump to $289.05 in fiscal 2028 (which will end in June 2028) and it continues to trade at 7 times earnings, its stock price could reach $2,023 in a year and a half.
